claims.statement: All bridges exact AND epoch-monotone implies closure preserved across the chain.
Pairwise exactness alone does NOT suffice: there exists a chain of exact bridges that loses closure under an ordering inversion.
On failure, the revalidation set is exactly the downstream affected closure.
Exactness and monotonicity are independent; each failure has a distinct location.

enumeration.bridge_patterns: every subset of adjacent bridges marked exact
enumeration.epoch_orderings: every assignment of epochs from a small ordered set to the transforms, so monotone and non-monotone chains both occur

controls.statement: C2 asserts a countermodel EXISTS. The sweep must actually exhibit at least one all-exact non-monotone chain that loses closure. If none is found, C2 is unsupported and must be reported as such rather than quietly passing.
A planted chain with a non-exact bridge must be reported as losing closure by the SAME predicate used for real cases.
Every all-exact epoch-monotone chain must preserve closure and none may be flagged. A checker that alarms on the good case cries wolf.
C4 requires BOTH failure modes to occur separately: at least one chain failing only from inexactness with monotone epochs, and at least one failing only from ordering with all bridges exact.

conditions: C4's two failure modes both occur
terminals.licenses: A bounded statement that exactness and epoch-monotonicity are jointly sufficient and separately necessary for closure preservation over arbitrary finite chains.

conditions: some all-exact epoch-monotone chain loses closure
terminals.reading: The induction is wrong; chains need a stronger hypothesis than pairwise exactness plus ordering.

conditions: no all-exact non-monotone chain loses closure, or the two failure modes do not separate
terminals.reading: Epoch-monotonicity would then be decorative and the promotion's central content would evaporate — pairwise results would already give chains.

retrospective_evidence.consequence: NO FROZEN TEST IS RUN AGAINST IT.
retrospective_evidence.and_it_is_the_wrong_shape_anyway: that campaign measures PAIRWISE single-transition closure retention, not multi-hop chains, so it cannot supply the multi-hop evidence a chain promotion would require

stop_rule: Outcomes are read once. On T2 or T3 the lane stops. On T1 the theorem stands but no multi-hop real evidence exists, so ORION-17 remains bounded.
